note: storms: HURDAT2 (NOAA/NHC, public domain), hurricanes only. eruptions/quakes/weather: authored from general knowledge — VERIFY dates, magnitudes, tolls against Smithsonian GVP, USGS/ISC, and period press before v0.1.

eruptions.name: Sakurajima
eruptions.line: Sakurajima in eruption; lava reaches the sea at Kurokami. Kagoshima sweeps ash.

eruptions.name: Hekla
eruptions.line: Hekla erupts after a century's silence. Ash to thirty kilometres; the column is seen from Scotland.

eruptions.name: Cumbre Vieja
eruptions.line: The San Juan eruption opens on La Palma's Cumbre Vieja on the saint's day. Thirty-seven days; lava to the western coast.

eruptions.name: Mauna Loa
eruptions.line: Mauna Loa's largest eruption in a lifetime. Lava crosses the coast road in three hours.

eruptions.name: Etna
eruptions.line: Etna's longest flank eruption in living memory begins. Milo threatened.

eruptions.name: Lamington
eruptions.line: Mount Lamington explodes without warning. The Higaturu district is gone; 2,942 dead.

eruptions.name: Myōjin-shō
eruptions.line: A submarine volcano surfaces south of Tokyo and destroys the survey ship sent to study it. No survivors.

eruptions.name: Mount Spurr
eruptions.line: Spurr erupts; a quarter-inch of ash on Anchorage by afternoon.

eruptions.name: Ruapehu
eruptions.line: Ruapehu's crater lake bursts. The lahar takes the Tangiwai rail bridge with the Wellington express on it.

eruptions.name: Kīlauea
eruptions.line: Kīlauea's east rift opens through the cane fields of lower Puna — twenty-four vents in eighty-eight days. The coast from Kalapana to Kapoho evacuated.

eruptions.name: Kelud
eruptions.line: Kelud erupts in East Java, VEI 4. Ash on the rice terraces from Kediri to Malang.

quakes.name: Aleutian Islands
quakes.line: Aleutian earthquake, M8.6. The tsunami reaches Hilo five hours later, unannounced. 167 dead — most of them in Hawaii.

quakes.name: Samaná Bay
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.0 off the Samaná peninsula. The tsunami takes Matanzas; 1,800 dead.

quakes.name: Ancash
quakes.line: Ancash earthquake in the Peruvian Andes. Landslides bury the valleys; 1,400 dead.

quakes.name: Nankai
quakes.line: Nankai earthquake, M8.1. Tsunami along the Kii coast; 1,362 dead, 36,000 homes gone.

quakes.name: Fukui
quakes.line: Fukui earthquake, M6.8. The city, rebuilt after the war, is flattened again. 5,131 dead; 63,000 homes.

quakes.name: Ashgabat
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.3 under Ashkhabad. The Soviet press reports damage. The toll — 110,000 — will be a state secret for forty years.

quakes.name: Khait
quakes.line: Khait earthquake, M7.5, in the Tajik SSR. Landslides bury the valleys; 12,000 dead. Moscow says nothing.

quakes.name: Ambato
quakes.line: Ambato earthquake, M6.5. Mountain towns buried by landslides; 6,000 dead.

quakes.name: Assam–Tibet
quakes.line: Assam–Tibet earthquake, M8.6, among the largest ever recorded. Whole hillsides into the Brahmaputra; 1,530 dead. The river dams, then breaks.

quakes.name: Jucuapa
quakes.line: Jucuapa earthquake in El Salvador. The town levelled; 1,100 dead.

quakes.name: Tokachi
quakes.line: Tokachi earthquake, M8.1, off Hokkaido. The tsunami takes 2,400 homes along the coast.

quakes.name: Kern County
quakes.line: Kern County earthquake, M7.5 — the largest in the lower forty-eight in fifty years. Tehachapi in ruins; the Southern Pacific tunnels collapsed.

quakes.name: Kamchatka
quakes.line: Kamchatka earthquake, M9.0. Tsunami across the Pacific; Hilo flooded again. Severo-Kurilsk erased, 2,300 dead — Moscow does not report it.

quakes.name: Yenice–Gönen
quakes.line: Yenice–Gönen earthquake, M7.3, south of the Marmara. 1,070 dead.

quakes.name: Orléansville
quakes.line: Orléansville earthquake, M6.7. 1,243 dead in the Chélif valley.

weather.line: The worst drought since 1891 across the Ukraine and Moldavia. The harvest fails; Moscow exports grain anyway. A million will die by spring.
weather.unmade: The drought the Ukraine expected did not come. The harvest holds. Moscow exports anyway.
weather.worse: Drought across the Ukraine, worse than any on record. The villages stop reporting.

weather.line: The coldest winter in a century locks Britain in ice. Coal cannot move; the lights go out.
weather.unmade: A mild winter on the North Sea. The coal moves; the grid holds.
weather.worse: The worst winter in three centuries. Britain's coal is under snow; the ports freeze.

weather.line: Blizzards bury the Plains and the Great Basin. Operation Snowbound digs out Nebraska; Haylift's C-82s drop feed to a million cattle across Nevada.
weather.unmade: A dry, open winter on the Plains. The cattle come through.
weather.worse: The Plains blizzards do not stop. Herds lost by the hundred thousand; Haylift cannot keep up.

weather.line: The wettest year on record in New South Wales. The Hunter and the Macquarie over their banks for months.
weather.unmade: The rains that were forecast for New South Wales never arrive. A dry, ordinary year.
weather.worse: Floods in New South Wales beyond anything recorded. Maitland underwater a second time.

weather.line: The Brahmaputra, dammed by the earthquake's landslides, breaks through. Assam under water.
weather.unmade: The Brahmaputra stays low after the earthquake. Assam is spared.
weather.worse: The Brahmaputra floods on a scale no gauge can measure. Assam is an inland sea.

weather.line: The Kansas and Missouri rivers over their levees — the highest since 1844. The Kansas City stockyards under water; 518,000 displaced.
weather.unmade: The Kansas River stays in its banks. A quiet July.
weather.worse: The Kansas and Missouri floods run for weeks. Both cities' stockyards are gone.

weather.line: The North Sea storm surge breaks the dikes of Zeeland and the Thames sea walls. 2,500 dead in a night.
weather.unmade: The February gale passes over the North Sea without a surge. The dikes hold. Nobody knows how close it came.
weather.worse: The North Sea surge overtops every dike from Zeeland to the Humber. The count stops at five thousand.

weather.line: The fourth year of drought across Texas and the southern Plains — the worst on the state's record, and 1954 among its driest. Ranchers drive cattle north to Kansas; the drought follows them.
weather.unmade: The rains return to the southern Plains. The drought the almanacs feared breaks a year early.
weather.worse: The southern Plains drought deepens. Dust over Amarillo again, thirty years on.

weather.line: Typhoon Kathleen breaks the Tone and Arakawa levees. The Kanto plain under water; 1,077 dead, 850 missing.
weather.unmade: The September typhoon turns east of Honshu. The Tone holds.
weather.worse: Typhoon Kathleen drowns the Kanto plain to the edge of Tokyo. The count passes two thousand.

weather.line: Typhoon Ione ashore on Honshu after a Category 4 peak. Floods across the Kanto and Tohoku; 838 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ione passes offshore. Rain, and nothing more.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ione stalls over Honshu. The rivers of the Kanto go over their banks twice.

weather.line: Typhoon Kitty crosses the Kanto on the last night of August. Floods and landslides; 123 dead; fifteen billion yen.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Kitty weakens in the Sagami Sea. Tokyo gets a wet night.
weather.worse: Typhoon Kitty comes ashore on Tokyo Bay at full strength. The Kanto's rivers over their banks for the third year running.

weather.line: Typhoon Irma — the worst on Shanghai's record. Sixty-three thousand houses down; 1,600 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Irma recurves east of the Yangtze mouth. Shanghai is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Irma drives the sea into Shanghai. The Bund under water; the toll passes three thousand.

weather.line: Typhoon Jane across Shikoku and Kansai; the surge into Osaka Bay. 539 dead in the floods and slides.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Jane recurves short of Kansai. Osaka is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Jane puts Osaka Bay's surge into the city centre. The Hanshin industrial belt is offline for the quarter.

weather.line: Typhoon Ruth across Kyushu and Yamaguchi. Rivers over their banks; 572 dead, 221,000 homes, 9,600 boats.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ruth stays at sea. The harvest comes in.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ruth takes the rice harvest of western Japan on the ground. Rationing tightens.

weather.line: Typhoon Tess, a Category 5 at sea, ashore in Aichi. 393 dead; Tokyo missed by a swerve.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Tess recurves short of Honshu. Nagoya gets a gale.
weather.worse: Typhoon Tess holds its course into Tokyo Bay. The capital takes a super typhoon head-on.

weather.line: Super Typhoon Ida ashore in Chekiang, the strongest of the year. 884 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ida recurves toward the Ryukyus. The coast is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ida across the Yangtze delta at full strength. Shanghai's river wall breached.

weather.line: Typhoon Marie sinks the ferry Toya Maru off Hakodate. 1,361 lost, 400 missing; five ships down in a night; Iwanai burns.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Marie weakens in the Sea of Japan. The Hakodate ferries sail.
weather.worse: Typhoon Marie crosses Hokkaido at full strength after the Tsugaru Strait takes the ferries. Sapporo's harvest is flattened.

weather.line: The Yangtze at 29.7 metres at Wuhan — the highest on record — from June to September. Hubei under water; 33,000 dead with the plague that follows.
weather.unmade: The Yangtze stays in its banks. A wet year, not a fatal one.
weather.worse: The Yangtze breaks the Wuhan dike. The city is an island; the plain a sea.

weather.line: The winter of 1947. Berlin burns its furniture; the Rhine freezes; the potato clamps are ice.
weather.unmade: A mild winter across the plain. The clamps hold.
weather.worse: The winter of 1947, and worse: the canals frozen to April, the seed potatoes lost.

weather.line: The North Sea surge breaks Zeeland's dikes in the night. Eighteen hundred dead in the Netherlands.
weather.unmade: The February gale passes without a surge. Zeeland sleeps.
weather.worse: The surge tops every dike in Zeeland and South Holland. Rotterdam's cellars are under salt water.

weather.line: The Danube within a hair of the 1899 mark at Vienna. The Austrian and Hungarian lowlands under water into August.
weather.unmade: The Danube rises, and stops short of the quays.
weather.worse: The Danube takes the plain from Linz to Budapest. The harvest is under it.

weather.line: The Winter of Terror: 649 avalanches across the Alps. Andermatt hit six times in an hour; 265 dead, Austria and the Valais worst.
weather.unmade: An open Alpine winter. The passes stay clear.
weather.worse: Avalanches every day for a week from the Valais to the Tyrol. Whole villages dug out by hand.

weather.line: A tornado nearly two miles wide runs from the Texas panhandle through Woodward, Oklahoma. A hundred city blocks gone; 184 dead.
Waco, Flint, Worcester: three tornadoes in four weeks each kill more than ninety. The deadliest spring on record.
The Chinchaga fire, the largest in North America's record, burns from June to October. Blue suns over New York and Edinburgh; Toronto's streetlights come on at noon.
weather.unmade: A wet spring in the Peace country. The fire season never starts.
weather.worse: The Chinchaga fire and a dozen more. The northern plains under smoke till the snow.

weather.line: Christmas floods across the Central Valley. The Feather levee breaks at Shanghai Bend on Christmas Eve; Yuba City under twenty feet; 74 dead.
weather.unmade: A dry December in the valley. The reservoirs wait for snow.
weather.worse: The Feather and the Yuba take the whole north valley at Christmas. Sacramento's levees hold by inches.

weather.line: Polio's worst year: 57,000 cases across the United States. Swimming pools closed; the iron lungs are full.
Cholera out of al-Qurayn, through the Delta. A thousand cases a day by October; ten thousand dead by December.
The desert locust rises from the Red Sea coasts. The plague will run four years, from the Delta to the Punjab.
weather.unmade: The locust breeding grounds are dry. The swarms never form.
weather.worse: Locusts across the Delta, the Sahel and Arabia in numbers no one has recorded. The FAO calls it a plague.

weather.line: Floods, then a failed monsoon, across Bihar and Rajasthan. India tells Washington it must import six million tons of grain and cannot pay for two.
weather.unmade: The monsoon arrives on time in Bihar. The wheat loan is not needed.
weather.worse: The monsoon fails from Rajasthan to Bengal. The ration is cut to the bone.

weather.line: The Punjab rivers in flood together. Lahore's suburbs under water; the wheat sowing lost.
weather.unmade: The Punjab rivers stay low into October.
weather.worse: The five rivers of the Punjab flood at once. Lahore cut off for a week.
